properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/16/2023 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Fallowfield Township, Washington county. 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/16/2023
Violation Code: 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID: 8162889
Permit API: 125-22817
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/16/2023
Comments: On 10/16/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 10/12/2023 (IR 3630018, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Paul Stiner of Diversified. On 10/12/2023, violations of 91.34(A), 78.66(b), 78.57(a), 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.53, 102.11(a)1, and 102.22(a) were issued as outstanding for the observed elevated conductivity and the access road condition. The following was observed during inspection on 10/16/2023:The operator had removed impacted soils within the bottom portion of the berm, adjacent to the valve of tank 4. No elevated conductivity observed (Photos 1-6). The operator had placed the impacted soils within buckets that were dated (Photos 7, 8).Some soils were removed from the berm adjacent to tank 5. No elevated conductivity observed (Photos 9, 10).Regarding the area behind tank 5, it appeared as though the area I initially discovered to have elevated readings, and the operator was not able to replicate my readings, displayed adequate readings on 10/16/23, most likely due to dilution from rain (Photos 11, 12). There was one reading of 3.29 m/S, however this area was small, approximately a 4 inch by 4 inch section (Photo 13). The operator is going to remove some soils from this area, which was marked with a brick (Photo 14). Due to the size of this area, no violation is being noted.The operator explained that the cause of the impacted berm was due to fluids reaching the ground during tank clean out (Photos 15, 16). It is highly recommended to place containment/grate to collect any residual fluids and prevent them from reaching the ground and berm during tank clean out.The access road appeared to remain in poor condition (Photos 17, 18). On 10/13/2023, I had emailed Daniel Frick of Diversified regarding the start time of repairs; Diversified is waiting on bids and can hopefully update me next week (from 10/13 email). As of 10/16/2023, there has not been an update. Also in this email, I had asked if the NOV response for IR 3620008, mentioning the removal of a 5 gallon bucket, was referring to the area under the valve of tank 4 instead of behind tank 5, which was then confirmed to be correct - the material was removed from under the valve. Due to the operator's effort to remediate the impacted areas and the impacted areas appearing in relatively good condition, the violations of 91.34(A), 78.66(b), 78.57(a), 78.54, and SWMA 301, regarding the release of production fluid, are being closed. Violations of 78.53, 102.11(a)1, and 102.22(a), regarding the access road, remain outstanding.

Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess site conditions after a reported release of produced fluid on Pad A in November of 2021. properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 953718
Permit API: 125-28875
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Jefferson Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/02/2022
Comments: On May 2, 2022, I conducted an inspection of the MCC West Well Site in Jefferson Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a fluid release reported by the Operator on 5/1/2022. According to the report approximately 50-60 gallons of condensate oil was released to the well pad when a load line on a truck failed. The release was discovered on 5/1/22 at 8:10am and reported to the Department spill hot line on 5/1/22 at 9:46am. At the time of inspection, The Act 9 site ID sign was installed. The PPC plan and ER plan were on site. Three roll off disposal boxes were staged on the east corner of the well pad. The roll off boxes were labeled as Non-Hazardous Waste condensate impacted material and dated 5/1/22. The impacted area appeared to be directly adjacent to the brine tank secondary containment location. The impacted area appeared to be 40’ in length and approximately 15’ wide with a maximum depth of approximately 12 inches. No discharge was observed off the well pad and the spill did not appear to impact waters of the commonwealth. Violations are being issued for failure to control a regulated fluid resulting a release to the ground.

The quantity of oil spilled is unknown, but appears to be greater than 5 gallons and less than one barrel. Oil stained soil with absorbent peat is noted in an L shape approximately 10 feet wide and 30 feet long that extends to the edge of the location. Per the operator, the spill occurred over this past winter and the well pumper covered the spill with peat sorb, which then settled as it was not cleaned up as the winter went on. Spring melt allowed the material to run to the edge of the site. Per the operator, the employee is no longer with the company. Cleanup should be completed in the next few days. Followup inspection will be performed at that time.The operator was also asked about the steep and rutted access roads on this lease and said that they have recently acquired a new bulldozer and intend to grade and fix lease roads soon.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8159693
Permit API: 081-21880
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/19/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that on 9/18/23 a leak was discovered in a GPU on Pad A which led to the release of an unknown quantity of produced fluid to the pad surface. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad A. He showed me where the produced fluid leak occurred inside of GPU #3. He also showed me where the fluid overflowed the interior containment of the GPU and flowed outside of the GPU and onto the pad surface to the southwest of the GPU. A Waste Management crew was excavating the impacted area of the pad during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that the fluid appears to have traveled a couple of inches into the pad surface and then moved toward the southwest pad edge under the surface. A sump present in the stormwater channel along the southwest side of the pad had fluid in it with an electrical conductivity (EC) of 700 uS/cm. Mr. Subra stated that the initial EC reading taken in this sump was approximately 700 uS/cm and later it increased to approximately 1700 uS/cm. A smaller puddle of fluid approximately 25 feet to the north in the channel had an EC of 760 uS/cm during this inspection. No other fluid was observed in the channel or on the pad surface. The Department recommends vacuuming out the fluid in the southwest stormwater channel.Mr. Subra said that they plan to pursue Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Environmental consultant Penn E and R was present during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that Penn E and R were performing electrical conductivity screening and would take samples for the Act 2 remediation. Violations noted against permit 081-21855 for the produced fluid release to the surface of Pad A.Violations remain outstanding for the produced fluid release to Pad B from 2/21/23.

Comments: On 02/14/2020 WQS Kristof Eichenlaub conducted incident response inspection # 2999089 On 02/18/2020 at approximately 1350 I conducted a follow up inspection at the site. Foamer product and sediment laden water were discharging from the sediment basin outlet, overwhelming two silt socks, and discharging outside the LOD into UNT 8 to Frosty Run. The discharge caused accelerated erosion below the silt socks and extending into UNT 8 to Frosty Run. A contractor for Greylock was utilizing a bucket and a pressurized sprayer bottle in an attempt to remove foamer product from the sediment basin rip rap outlet. I inquired what the contractor was utilizing to eliminate the foam. The contractor informed me they were utilizing fabric softener. I contacted Greylock Regulatory Compliance Coordinator Keith Eighmey via phone, who indicated he was unaware of the contractor's activities. Eighmey indicated Greylock had previously utilized a defoaming agent in the channels and basin to eliminate foamer product. Eighmey indicated Greylock could provide the SDS for the defoaming agent. The Department requests Greylock provide the SDS for the defoaming agent. The spill had not been remediated and was continuing to discharge to UNT 8 to Frosty Run. A sediment laden water discharge to UNT 8 to Frosty Run was also continuing. Greylock discharged an additional substance to Waters of the Commonwealth during their attempt to remove the foamer. Some violations are ongoing as a result of a spill that was documented on 02/14/2020 (inspection # 2999089). Additional violations of CSL 301 and 307 have occurred due to Greylock discharging a chemical to UNT 8 to reduce the surfactant foam. A violation of OGA3259(2I) has occurred for failure to comply with DEP cleanup order issued on 02/14/2020.

Comments: I conducted a site inspection on the morning of July 27, 2026 with the property owner. The inspection was concerning a brine release that was reported to the Department on July 25, 2026 by Jim Stiffler of Apollo Resources. According to Mr. Stiffler, the property owner was moving a trailer on the evening of July 24, 2026 and hit a 3" flange on the brine tank with the trailer, resulting in a brine release of 3,200 gallons of brine fluids.During the inspection I viewed the production equipment and the brine release area. Sandy, wet soils, and dead vegetation was observed in the brine release pathway. Approximately 6" of brine fluids still remain in the 100 BBL brine tank. Brine fluids traveled approximately 64' from the brine tank and approximately 30' wide. An old filled in pit from when the well was drilled is located in the pathway of the brine release. I screened multiple soil locations using a Hanna soil probe. Conductivity readings >4.00 mS/cm were observed.A stream (South Fork Beech Creek) is located downslope of the well site. I screened the stream both upstream and downstream of the brine release, readings were 48 uS/cm upstream and 52 uS/cm downstream.Due to the amount of brine fluid's released/reported, the Department recommends pursing Act 2 for site remediation. Violations have been cited.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/17/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a third party report of crude oil accumulated outside of the tank battery located at this well site.Upon my arrival, I observed a steel stock tank within an earthen containment located behind a conventional well that is equipped with a pump jack. There are currently no appreciable accumulations evident inside of the containment. There is evidence of recent earth disturbance along the western wall of the earthen containment. Just beyond the west/southwest corner of the tank battery, aged crude oil is present over an approximate 50' path of varying widths across the forest floor. At this time, there is no active discharge and the released product appears to have remained within an isolated swale/low lying area. It appears that the source of the product originates from the vicinity of the tank battery, however with the well being in close proximity, the source of the released crude oil is currently unclear. No watercourses appear to have been impacted by this release.Stuart Morris of Pennhills was contacted after this inspection and I relayed my findings to him. Stuart was not aware of any releases from the tank battery, but he did state that the well was recently serviced. Pennhills intends to investigate the matter and begin cleanup operations.It is requested that Pennhills provide an explanation of what occurred on the well site to result in the crude oil release in their response to the Notice of Violation (NOV) that is included in this inspection report. Please note other information that is requested in the NOV.Upcoming inspections will be conducted to evaluate the status of cleanup efforts and to review or further investigate the source of the release.

Comments On 6/16/2016, I performed an inspection of Rice Energy's Jacobs well pad site. Present at time of inspection was Jared Holman (Rice Company Man). The site is located in Gray Twp., Greene County. The inspection was performed as a incident inspection related to a reported brine spill by the operator. The operator reported a spill of approx. 1 barrel of produced water off of containment to the well padon 6/3/16. I met w/ Jared Holman, the Rice Drilling Consultant on site to review the incident. Mr. Holman stated that Rice personnel had removed impacted material from the well pad for disposal. Cudd Energy Services where on site completing coil tubing operations on the Jacobs 11H well, when a produced fluid line had ruptured and discharged produced fluid to the secondary containment on site. Cudd did not report this spill to containment and then parked a truck on the containment berm causing the produced fluid to discharge on the well pad. During the inspection water was observed pooling in the secondary containment at the location of the 6/3/16 spill. The water in the containment was inspected using a conductivity meter, which had a conductivity of 2.8 mS. Using a soil probe in the excavated impacted material location, conductivity readings ranged from 3.0 mS - 5.8 mS. Rice is recommended to move any equipment, and immediately begin a full site characterization to determine the extent of contamination resulting from the brine spilled to the site. Any remediation activities should be conducted in accordance with the Department’s Technical Guidance Document titled, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Roads (document number 800-50000-001). Rice is also recommended to monitor any nearby receptors such as streams, springs, ponds, ground water or water supplies for pollution caused by the spill.

Approximately six inches of material was scraped. Remediation will resume once the produced fluid tank is removed. The produced fluid tank will be removed either today or tomorrow. Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted after the operator reported a release of produced fluid to the surface of Pad A from GPU #3 on 9/18/23. Some fluid was present in the channel which had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 910 uS/cm. On Pad A, an area of secondary containment has been set up for the excavated pad material. Six GPUs are present and appear to be in good condition.On Pad B, nine wells are staged for production. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. Multiple batteries of frac tanks are present on the pad within secondary containment. A few puddles of fluid are present on the pad surface in front of the frac tank batteries which had an EC between 2.40 to 2.50 mS/cm. The Department recommends vacuuming up the fluid. The EC of the fluid in the sump at the east end of the north stormwater channel has an EC of 1645 uS/cm.Along the access road, vegetation has germinated where excavation took place after a truck rollover caused a release of produced fluid to an area surrounding the access road. The area is not yet permanently stabilized. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21855 for release of produced fluid to the surface of Pad A from 9/18/23.Violations remain outstanding for the release to Pad B from 2/21/23.

Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Deerfield Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/19/2021
Comments: Well continues to vent gas. The rate of venting does not appear to have diminished or increased. Gas concentrations of 100% volume were found in the casing vent. Gas concentrations of 8% fluctuating to 50%,(.04%-2.5% volume)were found in the headspace of the open surface casing. Cement plugs have not stopped the vertical flow of gas within the well bore as required by 25 PA Code, Chapter 78, 78.91(a). Remedial action will be required in order to properly plug the well and completely stop the vertical flow of gas within the well bore. Contacted company representative Tom Leonhortt at 09:30 on 5/19/2021. The contractor who performed the plugging procedures is currently working another job, and will not be available until the current job is finished. Mr. Leonhortt has contacted the contractor regarding the leaking gas to surface, and will keep me informed as to a date when the rig will return. Mr Leonhortt and I discussed options for remediation upon the contractors return. Some of these options included flushing out the top hole material, drilling out the casing seat plug, and running a downhole camera to determine the origin of the gas leak.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 12/14/2022
Comments: On Wednesday, 12/14/2022, I conducted a routine inspection of the Diversified Production, LLC McIntyre 1 well, permit number 005-29235. The well is located in the woods off of Coal Bank Road in Gilpin township, Armstrong county. The well is in production and had a reported production of 5,341.89 mcf for 2021. There is a well id tag attached to the well head and a well site id sign is posted on the production chart box. The site is restored, but the operator has not maintained the E and S BMP's for the site and there is an area of standing/ponded water on the access road near the site entrance (see picture #8) that needs to be addressed. The site cannot be considered stabilized due to this area and also the area of dead vegetation that was caused by brine being sprayed from a broken pipe onto the brine tank and ground. The brine tank itself is stable and appears to be structurally sound, but the pipe into the brine tank from the gas separator has rusted through and broken off, spraying brine onto the outside of the tank and onto the ground (see pictures #6 and #7). The amount of brine released appears to be less than 1 bbl. These conditions have resulted in violations to 25 PA Code 78.57(a), 25 PA Code 78.54, SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1) and CSL 402(b) being cited. Although there were no violations cited, the deficiencies on the access road need to be addressed while the operator is addressing the conditions that resulted in the cited violations.

Comments: On 07/20/2022, The Department received a call from Brian Haner, stating a tree had fallen on a the well overnight and had broken the gathering lines. There was crude getting into a unnamed tributary of Irvine run. An estimated 2+ barrels made its way off site. Upon arrival on site Mr. Haner had booms across the unnamed tributary in several locations. There was a small under flow dam built on a spring seep just below the well. There were also several booms placed at the mouth of the unnamed tributary to Irvine run. Oil absorbent pads were being used to collect oil behind the booms. The crude made its way from the well pad down to a spring seep approx 10-15 feet. The crude continued down the spring into an unnamed tributary of Irvine run approx 140 feet. The spill then continued down the unnamed tributary approx. 1/4 mile. There is some evidence of crude in Irvine run at this time but it is slight. Rain is predicted over the coming days. We spoke with Mr. Haner about placing some booms in a better suited areas. Rain is predicted and the unnamed tributary is prone rise very quickly with small amounts of precipitation. The unnamed trib channel is boulder strewn and very rocky. He said he would move the booms around and monitor them going forward. Mr. Haner also had a excavator in route. He was going to get the impacted soil nearest the well dug up and into containers. He was also going to better construct the underflow dam that was built in the spring flow area just below the well pad. The under flow that was built was functioning but with any appreciable amount of rain it may not handle the added flow.

Inspection Date: 4/22/2026
Comments: On April 22 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 3265061 of the OGM 1 OG Well.The findings were as follows:At the time of inspection, site ID sign (Act 9) was installed at the access road. The access road appeared stable with no observed accelerated erosion or sedimentation concerns. The well appeared equipped for production. No fluid leaks are observed around the well head and associated equipment. A well tag was present, however appeared to have incorrect operator information. Additional comments and violations regarding the well tag are documented under inspection report 4188085. The GPU appeared to be in sound condition with no fluid leaks or discharges observed.In the Department's previous inspection on 5/15/2025 (IR 3979004), elevated conductivity readings were obtained in an area of a suspected release near the production tank. In a follow up inspection conducted by the Department on 11/3/2025 (IR 406739) a roll of dumpster from McCutcheon Enterprises was on site and appeared to be full. There appeared to be fresh gravel in the location of previously elevated conductivity readings/suspected release area. The Department obtained conductivity readings in similar locations of the previously elevated readings and obtained readings of 0.05mS, 0.09mS, and 0.07mS. These readings were comparable/lower than the background conductivity reading of 0.14mS.At the time of today's inspection, the previously observed roll off dumpster appeared to be removed from the site. Conductivity readings in the locations of previously elevated readings appeared comparable to the readings obtained in the Department's 11/3/2025 inspection with readings of 0.06mS, 0.10mS, and 0.05ms obtained.The Department received a response from the operator on 5/29/2025 stating: "We will inspect site and check soil for possible need of removal". The Department has not received any further communication regarding remediation of the release.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for/or how remediation of the release was conducted. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection violations under IR 3265061 will remain outstanding for the release pending receipt and review of the requested information.
